data.narrative:
Periodic Labs is a seed-stage AI & Software company founded by Liam Fedus and Ekin Dogus Cubuk that has raised $300M to date. The target operates within a sector populated by 16 peer companies, including 1 public comparable (Palantir) and 8 private peers such as Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, and Reflection AI.

Valuation analysis employs stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($300M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to the next development stage yields an implied valuation of $750M. This method reflects observed progression patterns in frontier-tech funding rounds, though relies on the assumption that raised capital correlates meaningfully to post-seed valuation multiples.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum sample thresholds (0 same-stage peers, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier peers identified; analysis requires ≥3 datapoints). While a broader AI & Software peer universe exists, anchoring to all-sector medians would introduce material noise given Periodic Labs' specialized positioning.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $638M to $862M, centered on $750M. Key uncertainties include the adequacy of capital-raised proxies for early-stage valuation and the absence of narrow peer comparables, both of which constrain precision. Updated financials, revenue data, or a narrower peer set would materially improve confidence in this range.
